title: Economy: a number that grows between answers
note: Claims checked against an evidence pack, one checked figure that holds, a changed number, a question dodged across an ad break, applause, and a cue.

evidence.subject: growth
evidence.text: GDP growth over the last four quarters 1.2%

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Chancellor, let's start with the economy. How fast is it growing?

turns.speaker: CHN
turns.text: Growth this year is 3 percent, the fastest in the G7.

turns.speaker: ECO
turns.text: That is not what the official figures say.

turns.speaker: CHN
turns.text: Unemployment is at 3 percent, a record low.

turns.speaker: CHN
turns.text: Inflation is falling. It is at 2.6 percent and we expect it to keep falling.

turns.speaker: ECO
turns.text: Can I come back on growth? Chancellor, a moment ago you said growth was 3 percent.

turns.speaker: CHN
turns.text: Growth is running at 5 percent, as I said.

turns.speaker: ECO
turns.text: So which is it, Chancellor, three or five?

turns.speaker: CHN
turns.text: The point is that the economy is stronger than when we took office.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: We have to take a short break. Back in two minutes.

turns.speaker: AD
turns.text: Switch your energy today and save up to 200 pounds a year. Terms and conditions apply. Visit brightpower dot com.

turns.speaker: AD
turns.text: This programme is brought to you by Halden Insurance.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Welcome back. Let's talk about taxes. Chancellor, will you raise income tax?

turns.speaker: CHN
turns.text: We have no plans to raise income tax.

turns.speaker: ECO
turns.text: No plans is not a no.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Hepta, can you check the numbers we've heard tonight?
